findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no CFPM present during the beginning of the inspection. CFPM arrived mid-inspection. Ensure facility has a CFPM during all operational hours. Ensure the facility has more than one CFPM to cover all hours. Facility has multiple CFPM’s (see licenses in report). Ensure proper staffing to have a CFPM during all operational hours. Discussed with manager/CFPM who came to facility mid-inspection. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed multiple moths in the dry storage/storage areas (walk-in cooler/freezer is defunct and used as a dry storage area and a storage supply area) - at least 10 moths were present. Discussed with PIC. Inspector instructed PIC to call Orkin. Moths or any bugs should not be present in dry storage. Inspector will follow-up on 2/2/24.

Observed the following areas to be in need of repairs:
1. Light shield is cracked in the kitchen (and has dust) - replace.
2. Ceiling tiles need replaced throughout the kitchen - old, some are torn and/or missing.
3. Wall in front of the prep cooler is missing paint in various places - no longer smooth and easily cleanable.
4. Flooring needs replaced in kitchen (see General Comments).
5. The toilet paper dispenser has been replaced in the men’s bathroom and there is an area where the old one previously was - exposed and wall needs replaced.

Discussed repairs with PIC. PIC stated the facility plans to renovate the bathrooms then move into the kitchen. Ceiling tiles/light shields will be repaired first, then flooring. Walls of kitchen should be addressed at this time as well. Correct by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Both lids on the prep cooler are observed to be in disrepair. Inner sections of lids separate from the main body of the lid when lifted. The right lid also has silver tape that appears to have been used to attach/seal the lid in the past. This measure has failed ass the tape has broken along the seam of the lid. Inspector discussed that tape is general not an acceptable repair tool around moisture/foods. The lids need to be repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival no sanitizers were prepared and available for use. Inspector instructed the PIC to maintain available sanitizers at all times that the facility is in operation. A solution was produced using bleach during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

Multiple Foodborne Illness Risk Factor Violations noted on the report.PIC should be aware of critical control points related to the food establishment's procedures and how to remedy them. Education took place during the inspection.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

No CFPM is available at the facility during the inspection. As a Medium Risk Establishment, this facility must have a CFPM at the facility at all times that there is active food handling or handling of food contact surfaces taking place. PIC is instructed to ensure that a current CFPM is at the facility at all times of operation. A hand out for current CFPM courses was given to the PIC to facilitate training.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

PIC at the time of the inspection was not aware of any documentation related to employee illness documentation. Copies of reporting agreements given by SCDPH were given to the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all employees are aware of the content and sign.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

The bottom of the ice shoot on the fountain drink machine is observed with accumulated black slime/ mold. Due to the location there is a significant concern of the moist observed at this location carrying contaminants into drinks/ cups as ice is dispensed. PIC is instructed to clean/ sanitize surfaces related to foods often enough so as to prevent potential contaminants from landing in RTE foods. The location was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf). 

The bleach observed at the facility does not have an EPA registration number. Bleach in question is also a low splash variety as well as not having instructions related to sanitizing food contact surfaces. PIC is instructed to ensure that chemical sanitizers used in the facility meet requirements put forth by the 2017 FDA Food Code. Labels should include both EPA Registration Number as well as instructions for making a solution intended for food contact surfaces. Inspector will follow up in 10 days for compliance.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

The blade of the can opener is observed soiled during the inspection. PIC is instructed to clean/ sanitize the food contact surfaces after use to prevent accumulation of filth. Can opener was moved to the three part sink for washing during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

1) The pizza prep cooler is without an independent thermometer. 2) The standing cooler next to the hand sink is without an independent thermometer. PIC is instructed to ensure that thermometers are available to verify temperatures in the coolers are being maintained at appropriate levels. Inspector will follow up in 10 days for compliance.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. In the walk in cooler, observed containers (cottage cheese) that were opened but not date marked. PIC remedied on site.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed a open jar of pesto be sitting out at room temperature on a shelf above the pizza prep cooler.  Once pesto is opened, it shall be refrigerated and the label states, "Refrigerate after Opening".  The jar was discarded during inspection.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 140°F or above)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed the cutter used to cut dessert pizza to be heavily soiled with food debris and sitting up on the pizza oven, as observed at last inspection. This cutter was not cleaned from the night before and could potentially be contaminated with spoiled food or even pests since it sat out all night without being washed.  At the end of every night, all utensils used for food shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent the contamination of food.  The cutter was placed in the sink to be washed during inspection.
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of Comet to be stored on the top of the prep cooler that has food stored on top of it.  The bottle was moved to a proper location during inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of date labeling on the shredded cheese in the walk-in cooler and on pizza sauce in a container in the prep cooler.  Label all PHFs with the date when they have been prepared or removed from their original packaging.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the cheese stored on top of the prep cooler on the right to be at 70 degrees F and the items inside the cooler were at 70-75 degrees F.  The cooler was unplugged by accident and all potentially hazardous food (PHFs) inside were discarded during inspection.  The unit was plugged back in and will not be filled again until it is at 41 degrees F or lower.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 140°F or above)

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Prep cooler located on the right side in the kitchen was accidentally unplugged, due to the handsink being behind the unit, where it is plugged into the wall.  The unit was plugged back in and will not be filled again until it is holding at 41 degrees F or lower.  All PHFs inside unit were discarded during inspection.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed two small pizza/dessert cutters to be stored soiled on the pizza oven, to be used again for cutting food.  The cutters had sat their soiled all night and the surface they were stored on was also soiled.  Clean the surface where the cutters are stored and wash, rinse, and sanitize all equipment and utensils nightly, do not store soiled.
750.120a: At all times, food shall be protected from potential contamination including unclean equipment and utensils.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled:  1. inside of lids on pizza prep cooler  2. plastic piece inside ice machine  3. pliers used to remove pizzas from the pizza oven  Clean and sanitize the above mentioned items.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled:  1. racks inside the walk-in cooler  2. fan cover and area around fan, including the ceiling in the walk-in cooler  3. wall behind pizza prep cooler  4. inside the cooler on the right  5. side of scale on the prep cooler  6. shelf holding the pizza boxes  7. powdered sugar container  8. edge of pizza oven  9. hood vent filters  10. caulking along the 3 part sink has mold due to leak at chemical hose connector  11. ledge of ice machine by the lid  12. 3 gray bus tubs under the shelving by dish area  13. dish racks storing clean and dirty dishes  14. top of pipes and electric box located under the table next to the 3 part sink  Clean the above mentioned items.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the hose connector for the chemicals located on the 3 part sink. Repair the leak at this connector.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed a gap at the back door around the deadbolt and along the right side of the door.  Repair the door so that the lock and the door are tight-fitting, not allowing any sunlight to be visible.  A follow-up inspection will be conducted in 30 days to see that the door has been repaired.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
*Observed the floor to be soiled along the wall next to the tanks and the ice machine.  Clean the floor in this area.
*Observed the coving/baseboard to be loose, missing, or have spray foam on it along the wall to floor joint in the dish area and pizza oven area.  Repair or replace the coving in this area and anywhere else in facility where it needs attention, so that the floor to wall juncture is smooth, easily cleanable, and tight-fitting.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
*Observed a hole in the wall by the chemical dispenser in the mop closet and a hole in the wall in the women's restroom where the door knob has hit the wall.  Repair the holes in the walls.
*Observed the wall to be soiled behind the prep cooler and above the table between the ice machine and the 3 part sink. Clean the walls in these areas.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
